analysis:
This batch is documentation only: the configuration.md tail (cluster console, chunk policy, Qwen TP, stop intent), the new docs/reports/2026-10-31-public-cluster-models.md, and a reports/README.md index line. No executable code, wire protocol, key handling or authorization logic changes in the supplied units, so I found no concrete regression.

The security-relevant content is documentary. The new report records an owner decision to declare GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B for public cluster traffic in pipeline and tensor-parallel modes. It says releases carry pair-serving grants and parity qualifications (`cluster_runtime`) that a coordinator may derive approvals from. It states the evidence is not a hosted-provider certification and that no pipeline run on two M5 Ultras and no GLM tensor-parallel bundled record exist. The qualification rests on the owner's ruling and DevNet results. That matters for TB-011, T-052, T-054 and A-017: the report itself says it records an owner decision, not a durable independent qualification.

Open integration questions I could not verify from the supplied evidence: (1) the Swift `ClusterPublicModels`, `ClusterPairServingGrants` and release `cluster_runtime` registration code. These are in other batches, and the truncated configuration.md patch excerpt hides the earlier changed ranges (lines 923-1104). (2) Whether the coordinator-side derivation of grants from a release block is gated on authenticated release registration (A-005). Platform-owned code is out of scope here. (3) Whether `evidenceSHA256` binds to this file's content as claimed. The threat model may need an update, since the public-model gate and grants derived from releases are new trust inputs under TB-011/A-017. The earlier configuration.md hunks and the Swift code deserve review in their own batches.
